title: Driven on the keg: at new's argument order, the intent@2 remedy no tap has, and a pre-v2.10 project told there is no project
body:
From dc's keg drives:

- `at new` fails in the argument order its usage prints, because the `--covers` variadic swallows the ids.
- A project stamped below v2.19.0 is told to `install intent@2`, which no tap has.
- A pre-v2.10 project (a top-level `.intent/`) is told "no Intent project found" (`project.rs:866`).

Line numbers as at the audit.

Found by hv's estate-wide doc audit of 2026-09-11 (the audit's orders are in `intent/history/20260911-doc-audit.md`), where it is described as built. Carried in `intent/wip.md` as an unruled defect until 2026-09-13, when that file was leaned and every open defect became an issue. Not worked until hv rules it; a ruled one gets a lane.


CLOSED 2026-09-14 (dc), all three:
- `at new` in usage order was already fixed by 0305. Re-driven on this build: `ok: AT-01.2 created` (scratchpad batch/judge-0333.txt).
- Below the v2.19.0 floor, the remedy names the v2.19.0 release and its URL, then v2.19.0's own `intent upgrade`, then v3's, and no longer the `intent@2` no tap has. `upgrade_command` and `unmigrated_project` assert the release text; both pass on 3fbdd4ca0 with the fix (batch/judge-keg-tests.txt, 17:31:05Z: 5 and 11).
- A pre-v2.10 project (a `.intent/config.json` layout carrying `intent/st` or `stp`, the user-state home excluded) is `ProjectError::PreV210`, and the CLI prints that error's own remedy where it used to hardcode "run `intent init` here". Judged on a pre-v2.10 fixture (batch/compile-e705.txt, 16:18:29Z): "is an Intent project from before v2.10 ... remedy: bring it to v2.19.0 with Intent v2.19.0 first (the v2.19.0 release: https://github.com/matthewsinclair/intent/releases/tag/v2.19.0, then its `intent upgrade`), then run `intent upgrade` with v3".
